summary: Short turn spent resolving one concrete premise the open sweep gap depends on rather than padding with activity. Reading storage.go established that a restarted raft instance in this snapshot adopts its configuration only from Storage.InitialState's ConfState: newRaft feeds that ConfState to confchange.Restore, MemoryStorage.InitialState returns the snapshot metadata's ConfState (via pb.EnsureConfState), and that ConfState changes only when the caller supplies one - ApplySnapshot installs the given snapshot (including the snapshot-only-ConfState bootstrap case when the stored index is 0) and CreateSnapshot copies the caller's cs parameter - while Append and Compact never touch the metadata. Consequence for the next case: a restart in the randomized sweep cannot expect MemoryStorage to track configuration changes it appended; the harness must carry the applied ConfState forward itself, which is exactly the documentation's application duty, so the sweep's restart event needs that plumbing before it can be requested. Recorded as a behavior knowledge entry with its two new source ranges and conditions; the sweep gap (simple and joint configuration changes, learner promotion, and restarts from persisted storage, plus whether the campaign guard's applied-lag condition can leave a cluster without an electable voter in that wider event set) remains open and unanswered, and no experiment was requested because the wider sweep case is still unbuilt.
